description: Utqiaġvik (Barrow) Sea Ice Radar and Webcam is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by University of Alaska Fairbanks | Geophysical Institute | Sea Ice Group; Arctic Slope Regional Corporation; NSF, National Science Foundation. The Sea Ice Group at the University of Alaska Fairbanks' Geophysical Institute operates a coastal ice observatory in Utqiaġvik (formerly called Barrow), Alaska. The site displays data from a coastal webcam and radar. Various features on the site document conditions along Alaska's northern coast, and includes an archive of past conditions. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Extreme Cold, Flooding – Coastal. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife, Transportation and Mobility. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
